skill.name: managing-projects
skill.description: GitHub Projects v2 skill for creating and managing boards, fields, views, items, and automation workflows with GitHub CLI and GraphQL.
skill.summary: Manage GitHub Projects v2 boards, fields, views, items, and GraphQL workflows.
skill.author: C0ntr0lledCha0s

security_audit.summary: The skill is legitimate GitHub Projects v2 automation, but it includes privileged installation guidance and a helper that can execute scripts outside the audited package. Most Markdown examples, GitHub CLI snippets, official URLs, and /dev/null redirects were false positives; the remaining risks involve elevated host modification and unsafe shell execution patterns.

remediation.issue: Privileged package installation is described as automatic and shown with sudo commands.
remediation.suggestion: Remove automatic installation behavior. Ask for explicit user confirmation and link to official installation instructions instead of running sudo from the skill.

remediation.issue: project-helpers.sh resolves and executes setup scripts outside the audited skill directory.
remediation.suggestion: Keep dependency scripts inside the skill package or vendor them into the audited tree. Do not execute parent repository scripts implicitly.

remediation.issue: execute_with_retry uses eval on a constructed command string.
remediation.suggestion: Replace eval with array-based command execution, such as passing command arguments directly and invoking "${cmd[@]}".

remediation.issue: Several workflows can mutate live GitHub Projects data.
remediation.suggestion: Document side effects clearly and add dry-run or confirmation steps for bulk add, archive, delete, and field update operations.

content.value_statement: GitHub Projects v2 setup can require many GraphQL and CLI details. This skill guides board creation, fields, views, issue intake, and reporting workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides creation of GitHub Projects v2 boards with Kanban, Sprint, and Roadmap patterns.
Explains custom fields such as Status, Priority, Sprint, Size, Date, and Text.
Provides GitHub CLI and GraphQL examples for adding issues, pull requests, and project items.
Includes helper scripts for project queries, field updates, archiving, and reports.
Validates project configuration with a Python script that calls GitHub CLI.
Documents common GraphQL workarounds for Projects v2 operations.
limitations: Requires authenticated GitHub CLI access and project write permissions.
Some operations mutate GitHub project data and should be reviewed before execution.
Advanced setup examples may require jq, Python, or package installation.
Does not support classic GitHub Projects.

use_cases.title: Create Team Planning Boards
use_cases.description: Set up GitHub Projects v2 boards with useful fields, views, and workflows for active engineering work.

use_cases.title: Organize Release Work
use_cases.description: Track release issues, pull requests, priorities, and sprint status in one GitHub project.

use_cases.title: Audit Project Configuration
use_cases.description: Review project fields, item status, and view setup before standardizing board practices.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Board
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a small repository.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a GitHub Projects v2 Kanban board for OWNER with Todo, In Progress, Review, and Done.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Sprint Board
prompt_templates.scenario: Team sprint planning with custom fields.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a two-week sprint board for OWNER. Include status, priority, size, sprint, assignee, and target date fields.

prompt_templates.title: Add Issues with Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add matching issues to an existing project and set their status and priority fields safely.

prompt_templates.title: Build GraphQL Automation
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced automation for repeatable project operations.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GraphQL-based workflow to find project item IDs, update fields, archive done work, and report progress.

output_examples.input: Create a sprint planning project for my repository.
output_examples.output: A board plan with sprint fields, status columns, priority options, and a safe sequence of GitHub CLI actions.

output: Missing Priority field for triage decisions.
Roadmap view should use a target date field.
Done items older than the retention window can be archived after review.

output_examples.input: Move selected issues into a project and set status.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step workflow that finds issue node IDs, adds items, checks field options, and updates status values.

best_practices: Confirm the target owner, repository, and project number before running any mutating command.
Review generated GraphQL operations before applying them to production project boards.
Use dry-run planning and backups when bulk adding, archiving, or updating project items.
anti_patterns: Running privileged installation commands from the skill without explicit user approval.
Bulk updating project items before checking filters and field IDs.
Using classic GitHub Projects assumptions with Projects v2 GraphQL operations.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI?
faq.answer: Yes. Most workflows require an authenticated gh CLI session with access to the target project.

faq.question: Can it create GitHub Projects v2 boards?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides board creation guidance and templates for Kanban, Sprint, and Roadmap workflows.

faq.question: Can it manage project fields?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common field types and includes examples for field lookup and updates.

faq.question: Does it support Projects Classic?
faq.answer: No. The skill is focused on GitHub Projects v2 and its GraphQL API.

faq.question: Can it change live GitHub data?
faq.answer: Yes. Several workflows add, update, archive, or delete project items, so users should review commands first.

faq.question: Is setup fully automatic?
faq.answer: The skill includes setup guidance, but privileged package installation should require explicit user approval.
